other_human_context.author: u70b3
other_human_context.body:
Hi, I've been investigating this and have two results that may be relevant to your report.

**1. A deterministic crash (SIGSEGV) on 1.4.x/1.5.x in the same WAL profile family — root-caused, fix exists but no 1.5.x release contains it.** Synthesizing your WAL shape (un-checkpointed close/reopen cycles mixing `ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` + `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` + DELETE/INSERT) gives a 100%-reproducible SIGSEGV on every release build I tested (1.4.4, 1.5.3, 1.5.4, 1.5.5); assert builds abort even earlier, during WAL replay at open, with `INTERNAL Error: unbound_index.cpp:50 D_ASSERT(mapped_column_ids == mapped_column_ids_p)`. Root cause: replayed `CREATE INDEX` entries leave unbound indexes whose buffered replays latch the indexed-column-set mapping from the first buffered chunk (D_ASSERT-only guard, compiled out in release); when the WAL interleaves `ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN`/`CREATE INDEX` with row-data entries, later chunks carry a different mapping and the "row id" buffer column silently receives real column data (in my repro: NULLs), which is later fed to the ART as row ids → wild pointer dereference. Bisected on main to a single commit: **9613097434 "fix buffering for unbound indexes"** (#24038, 2026-07-21, ships in v2.0.0) — parent crashes, fix commit clean. The fix is already on the v1.5 maintenance branch too (backported by the author in #24326, 2026-07-31), but **no 1.5.x release tag contains it** (v1.5.0–v1.5.5 all predate it), so released 1.5.x binaries remain exposed — I've filed the details and a from-scratch minimal repro as #25928.

**2. Your exact symptom ("Conflict on tuple deletion" at replay) is a different defect — the crash above cannot produce it.** Your error is thrown from MVCC delete-state (`ChunkVectorInfo::Delete`); replayed DELETE row ids flow verbatim from the WAL with no index or column-mapping involvement, so the unbound-index corruption cannot reach it. Producing your error requires the replayed row-id space to diverge from the original execution — candidates are the optimistic-writer `ROW_GROUP_DATA` replay family (fixed on main in #24744, not in 1.4.x/1.5.x either) or a WAL being replayed over state that was already checkpointed.

Your offered `.duckdb` + `.wal` pair would settle it — since you offered to attach them: yes please. I'd dump the WAL entry sequence, compare the main file's contents against what the WAL adds, and check whether the pair trips the assert fingerprint above at open (which would tie it to the unbound-index bug after all). Also useful if easy: whether node-duckdb's close waits for the shutdown checkpoint, or whether the ~100 ms fire-and-forget gap means the WAL survived because close didn't run to completion.

comments.author: Tishj
comments.body:
I was not able to reproduce a crash with your example, I've built with v1.5.5 (hash d8cdaa33fda8df955cc76ef58a280f68f4cd43fa)

```
CORE_EXTENSIONS="spatial" make release
```

Built a sqllogictest:
```sql
statement ok
set custom_extension_repository = './build/release/repository';

statement ok
LOAD spatial;

statement ok
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE fire (
    ShooterId TEXT,
    MunitionId TEXT
);

statement ok
INSERT INTO fire VALUES ('2074', '2062');

statement ok
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE Detonation (
    ShooterId TEXT,
    MunitionId TEXT,
    Longitude DOUBLE,
    Latitude DOUBLE
);

statement ok
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE oparea (
    name TEXT,
    area TEXT
);

statement ok
INSERT INTO oparea (name, area)
VALUES ('xxxx', 'POLYGON((80 40,90 40,85 35,85 40,80 40))');

query III
SELECT
    Detonation.Longitude,
    Detonation.Latitude,
    IFNULL((
        SELECT FIRST(name)
        FROM oparea
        WHERE ST_Intersects(
            ST_GeomFromText(area), 
            ST_Point(Detonation.Longitude, Detonation.Latitude)
        )
    ), 'Other') AS area_name
FROM fire
LEFT JOIN Detonation
    ON fire.ShooterId = Detonation.ShooterId
    AND fire.MunitionId = Detonation.MunitionId
GROUP BY ALL;
----
NULL	NULL	Other
```

And also with the publicly distributed version of the `spatial` build (`INSTALL spatial;`) I wasn't able to get this to crash.

title: DuckDB inserting data violating non null constraint
context_note: Reference label observed; review opening context and human requests before freezing.

actual_maintainer_requests.summary: Maintainer samansmink requests a proper bug reproduction to establish a DuckDB-side problem; discusses a possible Parquet null-constraint limitation. This is a human comment, not only a bot response.

comments.author: samansmink
comments.body:
HI @joy13 thanks for reporting! 

DuckDB uploading partial data sounds wrong to me, since duckdb uses multi part upload which should mean that the files are either written completely or not at all.

What I think is happening here is that DuckDB is not setting the null constraints in the parquet files on copy, something that is a known limitation (See https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/issues/9476#issue-1962404618).

My suspicion is that you are somehow writing null values into the parquet files which then trigger the null constraint in your table.

So to investigate this further we'd need to have a proper bug reproduction which can demonstrates that this is actually a problem duckdb side
